headline: Chipmakers lift the Nasdaq 1.2% into Fed decision day as oil eases on Iran talks
subhead: The S&P 500 rose 0.6% to 7,722.6 and the 10 year yield sat near 4.99%, while WTI fell 1.1% to 100.7 dollars and the Nikkei gained 3.1% and the KOSPI 6.4% in Wednesday trade.

us.text: S&P 500 rose 0.6% to 7,722.60, Nasdaq 1.2% to 26,477.81, Dow flat at 52,377.57 as chipmakers led, SOX up 3.6%.
10-year yield edged up to about 4.995% as the Fed meeting began; futures price roughly 93% odds of a hold at 3.75% to 4%.
Week turns on the Fed decision Wednesday, Alphabet and Microsoft results Wednesday, Amazon Thursday, plus Q3 GDP and September PCE Thursday.

india.text: Nifty ended flat at 22,749.75 on Tuesday's F&O expiry as oil and Fed caution capped gains; pharma, realty and consumer durables outperformed.
FIIs were net buyers of about 4,240 crore rupees and DIIs net sellers of about 1,250 crore on 27 October, provisional exchange data.
USD/INR quoted at 95.1, down 0.1% in early Wednesday trade; no dated rupee close report was found this run.

global.text: Japan and Korea led Asia, with the Nikkei up 3.1% and the KOSPI up 6.4% in Wednesday trade; Hang Seng last closed up 0.5%.
STOXX 600 rose about 0.5% on Tuesday as lower oil and solid US data offset weak HSBC results, which weighed on London.
WTI fell 1.1% to near 100 dollars as Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish officials held Tehran talks on ending the Iran war; Hormuz tanker attacks continue.

weekly.narrative: Two forces ran the week and both pointed at the cost of capital. Attacks on shipping around the Strait of Hormuz, including Iranian claims that seven vessels were hit or mined, took Brent above 117 dollars and WTI past 100, and because that lands as an inflation shock rather than a growth scare it lifted rate expectations instead of safe havens: gold closed the week below 4,000 dollars and now sits 2.9 percent above its 52 week low and silver hit a year to date low, while the US 10 year held near 4.99 percent. The second force was the AI financing question, which moved from equity multiples to credit, with a Lam Research warning on chip supply into 2027 knocking the Nasdaq 2.6 percent on Thursday, CoreWeave 2032 bonds quoted near 78 cents on the dollar, and Jensen Huang arguing the sector is short of capital rather than demand. India inverted the pattern, with the Nifty pressured by the oil bill and foreign selling while IT rallied on a reverse AI trade that reads weaker AI capex as work returning to traditional services firms, and the rupee closed at 94.93 against the dollar. Next week stacks the catalysts: the Fed decision on 28 October with a hike priced near 7.6 percent, Microsoft and Alphabet that same evening, Amazon plus Q3 GDP and September PCE on 29 October, the Bank of Japan on 30 October, and in Mumbai the listing of the 30,213 crore rupee Jio Platforms issue alongside five new mainboard IPOs.
